week.worked: Haaland gave you 18 as captain and Kerkez kept a clean sheet at Ipswich, the one his trigger asked for. Cherki started beside Enzo Fernández and hit the post.
week.didnt: Elanga's first week in your side was 1 point, and Calvert-Lewin was put through twice at Brighton and scored neither. Five of your eleven play today, so the week is half written.

big.call: Captain: Haaland at Old Trafford or B.Fernandes at home to City
big.why: You own both and the derby is GW4. Haaland has scored in all three games and plays Porto away on the Tuesday before. B.Fernandes has three, all in one afternoon, and takes the penalties.

big.call: Palmer before Hull come to Stamford Bridge
big.why: Chelsea's next two are Hull at home and Brentford away. You have £0.7m in the bank, so he costs you B.Fernandes or a hit, in the week United host City.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Chelsea host Hull next week. You own two Chelsea players and he is neither of them. Read the Emirates first.

watchlist.name: Isak
watchlist.note: Three goals in two games at £9.0m and none of the five own him. You have Calvert-Lewin in that slot and he missed two one-on-ones at Brighton.

week.worked: Haaland gave you 18 as captain and Szoboszlai drove Liverpool's win from midfield. Your bench cost you nothing on Saturday.
week.didnt: You moved Groß into your eleven after his goal at Stamford Bridge and he put a six-yard chance over the bar for 1 point. Calafiori, B.Fernandes and João Pedro play today.

big.call: Captain with the lead: Haaland away or B.Fernandes at home
big.why: All five captained Haaland this week and he scored. Next week he goes to Old Trafford and you own the man who plays against him. If you match the room your lead can only shrink.

big.call: Calvert-Lewin off the bench for Leeds v Newcastle
big.why: He was put through twice at Brighton and missed both, but Leeds created 2.5 xG and host Newcastle at Elland Road next. It costs no transfer to fix.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: He made the Barnes goal from left-back against Bournemouth. You own two Coventry defenders you never start and no Newcastle player.

watchlist.name: Araujo
watchlist.note: Debut at right-back on Friday, a clean sheet and bonus points. Two more starts and he is a £5.4m route into Liverpool's defence.

week.worked: Gvardiol kept a clean sheet with the bonus, Kinsky kept Spurs' first of the season at Forest, and Ajayi has now not conceded in three games. You lead the room among those who held their chips.
week.didnt: E.Le Fée scored the penalty at Brentford on your bench while Hume gave you 1 on the day Danso made his Sunderland debut. Calafiori is on your bench again for Arsenal v Chelsea.

big.why: Arsenal go to Sunderland, Ajayi goes to Stamford Bridge and Hume hosts Arsenal with Danso now in the side. You own a 20-point defender and start two cheaper ones in front of him.

big.call: Captain: Haaland or B.Fernandes in the derby
big.why: You own both. Haaland goes to Old Trafford three days after Porto away and has scored in every game. B.Fernandes is at home and takes the penalties.

watchlist.name: Dewsbury-Hall
watchlist.note: Everton host United today. Moyes says the squad is short, and the creation left at the club runs through him.

watchlist.name: E.Le Fée
watchlist.note: He took and scored the penalty at Brentford. You own him and benched him behind Hume. Arsenal at home next, so read the Sunderland team sheet before promoting him.

week.worked: The Wildcard leads the room's gameweek by a distance, with three players to come. Gakpo made both Isak goals, Tzolakis and Egan kept a third clean sheet, and Gvardiol and Jacquet added two more.
week.didnt: Raya sits on your bench at £6.0m behind a £4.6m Hull goalkeeper. Tzolakis kept a clean sheet, so it cost nothing on Saturday. Arsenal play Chelsea at 4.30 and Raya's points go nowhere.

big.call: Raya off the bench: Hull go to Chelsea, Arsenal go to Sunderland
big.why: Tzolakis and Egan both play at Stamford Bridge next week. Arsenal have not conceded in three games this season, Community Shield included, and Raya sits behind a £4.6m keeper on your bench.

big.call: Captain: Haaland or B.Fernandes at Old Trafford
big.why: You are last of the five and you own both. Haaland goes to Old Trafford three days after Porto away. B.Fernandes is at home and takes the penalties.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: You wildcarded without your own club's penalty taker. Chelsea host Hull next week and he has 20 points in two games.

watchlist.name: Isak
watchlist.note: You own his supplier. Isak has five goals in three games at £9.0m and Liverpool host Fulham next.

week.worked: Egan kept a third clean sheet at £4.0m and Haaland gave you 18 as captain. Szoboszlai played in midfield at Ipswich, so your £7.0m did what it was bought for.
week.didnt: Kinsky kept a clean sheet on your bench behind Verbruggen, who conceded to Leeds' first chance. Cash kept one at Hull on your bench too. Rogers sits behind Tzolis for Arsenal v Chelsea.

big.call: Rogers off your bench: Chelsea host Hull
big.why: You bench a £7.5m midfielder who has started all three Chelsea games, and start Tzolis, who was hooked at half-time last week. Chelsea's next two are Hull at home and Brentford away.

big.call: Kinsky or Verbruggen: Everton at home, or Coventry away
big.why: Kinsky kept Spurs' first clean sheet at Forest and hosts Everton. Verbruggen goes to a Coventry side without a top-flight goal since 2001. You own both and one sits on the bench.

watchlist.name: White
watchlist.note: You own Calafiori and Tzolis and you do not own the Arsenal defender with 18 points. Mosquera is flagged for today and Sunderland away is next.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: 14 points at £6.6m and nobody in the room owns him. If Tzolis loses the left to Eze today, this is where the Arsenal money goes.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: 20 points in two, the penalties, Hull at home next. Nobody in the room owns him and two of the five support the club. Arsenal away at 4.30 is the test.

watchlist.name: Isak
watchlist.note: Three goals in two games and Iraola says he will produce the numbers if he is fit. £9.0m, and none of the five own him.

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: Two assists at Ipswich and the £123m winger came on for Muñoz, so the left flank is his. One of the five owns him.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: Made the Barnes goal from left-back with Burn out until mid-September. Leeds away next. None of the five own a Newcastle defender.

watchlist.name: Araujo
watchlist.note: Right-back on his league debut, ahead of Frimpong, with bonus points in Liverpool's first clean sheet. £5.4m, and the shirt needs two more starts.

watchlist.name: Scott
watchlist.note: 24 points in three games at £6.0m, and Rose says he is proud he is a Bournemouth player. Brentford at home next. Nobody in the room owns him.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Four of the five own an Arsenal defender and none owns the £6.6m midfielder who outscores them. Chelsea at home today, Sunderland away next.

watchlist.name: Konsa
watchlist.note: Nobody in the room owns him now. Mosquera has a 75% flag, Saliba is out for months, and Chelsea visit at 4.30 today.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: A hat-trick, the penalties, and all five own him. Carrick says United have five games in 16 days and he plays every one of them. Everton away at 2pm.
verdicts.trigger: Two quiet weeks with United losing. At £12.0m the price only works while he is the whole attack.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Got the fifth against Ipswich and held his flank all afternoon. Everton away today.
verdicts.trigger: Rashford keeping the left and the returns concentrating there. Two blanks and £7.9m is the wrong United winger.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: United signed no left-back, so the shirt is his. Carrick says rotation is inevitable with five games in 16 days, and Mazraoui is the back-up.
verdicts.trigger: Mazraoui starting a league game at left-back. That is the difference between a cheap defender who never misses and a rotation slot.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: Scored off a deflection and was the steady one in a defence that could have folded. Everton away today and City at home next.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-backs are fit. He starts every week until then.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Kept United in the Ipswich game with first-half saves and was the calm one in a panicked defence.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks conceding twice. You are paying £5.0m for a goalkeeper who saves shots and never keeps a clean sheet.

verdicts.name: Mainoo
verdicts.why: Carrick called his Ipswich performance immense and Baleba is out until mid-September, so the shirt is his for now at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts once Baleba is fit. Until then this is a cheap midfielder in a rotation Carrick has already promised.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: 20 points in two games, the penalties, and Chelsea sold Enzo Fernández without replacing him. Arsenal away at 4.30, then Hull at home.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide of the number ten, or the calf flag returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Owned by all five and the reference point in Chelsea's attack. The Emirates today is the hardest fixture on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box. At that ownership he is the risk.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Three starts from three since the £117m move, and Arsenal stopped at £80m for him. Two of his three owners in the room start him today, and Le Professeur benches him.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide right or on the bench. Nothing Alonso has said points that way.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: Chelsea have conceded five in two, have not kept a clean sheet in 18 games, and go to the Emirates today.
verdicts.trigger: One clean sheet. Hull at home next week is the first fixture where it is likely.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: Flagged at 75% and Chelsea expect him back for Hull at home, which is the week after the Emirates.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. Chelsea never replaced him and the shirt is waiting.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: 20 points at £5.7m, and Arteta says Arsenal can play with him stepping up more from left-back now the wingers have gone. Four of the five own him and Mr CR7 benches him today.
verdicts.trigger: The knee trouble that follows him around, or Arsenal's European calendar producing real rotation.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: The only goal at Villa Park, penalties at £9.5m, and Arsenal sold all three wide forwards who competed with him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or a January forward moving the returns centrally.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: 14 points at £6.6m and nobody in the room owns him. Arteta's plan for the season leans on him, Saka and Havertz staying fit.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or the returns concentrating in Saka alone.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: 18 points at £5.5m in a defence that has not conceded a league goal, and Mosquera carries a 75% flag for today.
verdicts.trigger: Timber getting past grass work and Saliba returning, which is not this side of the international break.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: The flag arrived on Saturday morning, two days after he missed open training. 75% for Chelsea, and nobody in the room owns him since The Special One's wildcard.
verdicts.trigger: A start today. If Konsa is named ahead of him this is a sack until Arteta says otherwise.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: Saliba is out for months, Mosquera is flagged, and the man signed to cover them is £4.4m. Le Professeur sold him on Friday instead of promoting him.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea today. He starts and this goes to solid.

verdicts.name: Raya
verdicts.why: Arsenal have won three from three this season without conceding, Community Shield included. His one owner in the room has him on the bench behind a Hull goalkeeper who has also kept three.
verdicts.trigger: Two goals conceded in a week. Chelsea today is the first attack that can test the number.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: The Guardian calls him Arsenal's most natural option on the left after four forwards went, and the club believe Eze can do the job too.
verdicts.trigger: A second half-time substitution, or Eze starting ahead of him against Chelsea today. Then it is a sack.

verdicts.name: Eze
verdicts.why: Arsenal believe he can replace Martinelli on the left, and he set up Saka's winner off the bench. £6.4m at 1.4% is the cheap way into the champions' attack.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea today. Give Arteta that team sheet and the price is wrong by a long way.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Trossard, Martinelli, Jesus and Nwaneri have all gone, so he and Gyökeres are the whole senior forward line.
verdicts.trigger: Gyökeres taking the shirt outright. Two games on the bench and £7.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Gyökeres
verdicts.why: Zero points in two at £7.3m, but he scored 21 last season and Arsenal are down to two senior forwards.
verdicts.trigger: A start and a goal in the next two. A £7.3m striker without a goal by GW5 is a sack.

verdicts.name: Bruno G.
verdicts.why: Flagged at 75% with a knock, one Arsenal appearance, and Merino and Zubimendi came off the bench at Villa Park ahead of anyone else.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea. Until then £6.8m buys a player nobody has seen finish a week fit.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Three goals in three games and his 300th in club football, from a Semenyo cross. All five captained him and all five got 18. Porto on Tuesday, then Old Trafford.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury. City bought no back-up, so there is no version of this where he plays less.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Clean sheet, bonus, and Maresca said the space on the left against Coventry was for him, with Ndiaye told to stay higher. Both his owners in the room start him.
verdicts.trigger: Doku back and City going wider with O'Reilly restored to defence. Nothing said this week points that way.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Started for the second week running, beside Enzo Fernández as one of two number eights, and hit the post. The trigger was two starts in a row and it has fired.
verdicts.trigger: A bench at Old Trafford after Porto on Tuesday. Foden was the one left out on Saturday.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: The trigger asked for a goal against Coventry. He got the assist for Haaland's winner and 6 points instead, from the right wing.
verdicts.trigger: A blank at Old Trafford. One assist in three at £8.4m and Ndiaye now shares the wide roles with him.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Back at centre-back against Coventry, a clean sheet and the bonus. The Guardian's report has him at centre-back. Nobody in the room owns him.
verdicts.trigger: Two league starts in midfield again. That is where a defender keeps no clean sheets.

verdicts.name: O'Reilly
verdicts.why: Felt his back in the warm-up on Saturday and Enzo Fernández took his place. Maresca says it is not serious and the file has him at 75%.
verdicts.trigger: Named in the derby squad. If he misses Porto and the derby, 17.8% of the game is holding a £6.5m absentee.

verdicts.name: Enzo
verdicts.why: Started on debut at number eight after O'Reilly's warm-up injury, made the goal with a pass to Semenyo, and came off for Bouaddi on 76. £6.9m at 3.3%.
verdicts.trigger: Two more starts once O'Reilly is fit. Maresca said he was on the bench only because he arrived days ago.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Sacked on Monday as squad depth. He started at the Etihad on Saturday, attempted more dribbles than anyone, and Maresca spent the press conference explaining what he did wrong.
verdicts.trigger: Doku fit and starting on the left. Doku's return date in the file was 5 September.

verdicts.name: Foden
verdicts.why: On the bench against Coventry while Ndiaye started on debut. One point.
verdicts.trigger: A start in the derby. Until then £7.0m for a substitute at his own club.

verdicts.name: Isak
verdicts.why: Two goals inside ten minutes at Ipswich, three in two games, and Iraola says he will produce the numbers if he is fit. £9.0m and none of the five own him.
verdicts.trigger: A week of managed minutes. He came off on 64 with the game won and Liverpool have Atlético on Wednesday.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: Thursday's trigger was Barcola starting on the left. Barcola started on the bench, Gakpo set up both goals and got a 9 from the BBC.
verdicts.trigger: Barcola starting ahead of him against Fulham. 28 points at £7.1m are real, and the shirt is his until a team sheet changes it.

verdicts.name: Barcola
verdicts.why: On the bench at Ipswich, on for Muñoz on 64, a 5 from the BBC. £123m does not buy the shirt by itself.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts on the left. At £8.0m he needs the shirt, and the first team sheet went the other way.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Played in midfield at Ipswich with Araujo at right-back, drove the game, and the BBC's man at Portman Road wrote that Iraola should never use him at right-back.
verdicts.trigger: One game at right-back. Three of the five own him at £7.0m for the penalties and the runs from midfield.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: The trigger was a clean sheet at Ipswich or against Fulham. It came at Ipswich, with 90 minutes and a 6 from the BBC.
verdicts.trigger: Conceding twice against Fulham at home. Then the Ipswich sheet was the promoted side and the price is the problem again.

verdicts.name: Jacquet
verdicts.why: Started beside Van Dijk in Liverpool's first clean sheet, and the BBC calls him a very fine acquisition. £5.0m at 2.6%, owned by The Special One.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the place to Konaté when he is fit, or two games conceding twice.

verdicts.name: Araujo
verdicts.why: Right-back on his league debut, ahead of Frimpong, with bonus points and a 7 from the BBC. Liverpool failed to sign a right-back and this is who they had.
verdicts.trigger: Two more starts there. At £5.4m he is a buy the moment the shirt is his.

verdicts.name: Frimpong
verdicts.why: Unused substitute at Ipswich while a centre-back made his debut at right-back.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. Until then £5.4m is a bench place.

verdicts.name: Wirtz
verdicts.why: Busy but lightweight at Ipswich, in the BBC's words, and 9 points from three games at £7.4m.
verdicts.trigger: A goal or an assist against Fulham. The Guardian says the internal competition is after his spot if not.

verdicts.name: Elanga
verdicts.why: Started on the right against Bournemouth and his flick-on made Willock's chance, but 1 point. Fernandez-Pardo made his debut at number ten, behind Wissa and away from Elanga's flank.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo moving wide. He was used at ten on Saturday, so the flank is still Elanga's.

verdicts.name: Wissa
verdicts.why: Started as the lone striker against Bournemouth and crossed for Willock's near miss, but 1 point. Fernandez-Pardo came on behind him, so the shirt is his.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo being played centrally, or two blanks in the easiest run in the league.

verdicts.name: Hall
verdicts.why: Made the Barnes goal from left-back with the pass the Guardian called intelligent. Burn is out until mid-September and none of the five own him.
verdicts.trigger: Burn returning around 14 September and the left side going back. Until then he is the cheapest attacking defender at a settled club.

verdicts.name: Barnes
verdicts.why: Cut in from the left and curled in the goal that started the comeback. 17 points at £6.0m and 1.4% own him.
verdicts.trigger: A second goal in the next two. The Guardian called him frustrating until the moment he scored, and Fernandez-Pardo cost £51m to play near him.

verdicts.name: Dedić
verdicts.why: Started at right-back against Bournemouth with Livramento on the bench, and Newcastle conceded two goals Jaissle called slapstick. 1 point at £4.5m.
verdicts.trigger: Livramento fit and starting. A £4.5m defender who keeps the shirt through that is a buy.

verdicts.name: Tzolakis
verdicts.why: Three clean sheets in three at £4.6m, and Hull have had 29% of the ball. Villa managed one shot on target and he saved it.
verdicts.trigger: Hull conceding in both of the next two. Stamford Bridge is the first real test.

verdicts.name: Ajayi
verdicts.why: Part of a back three that has not been breached, and Egan says the shape dates from the play-offs. Mr CR7 bought him this week.
verdicts.trigger: Norton-Cuffy starting at right-back. Jakirovic says the cup tie on Tuesday is where the new arrivals get minutes.

verdicts.name: Egan
verdicts.why: Three clean sheets at £4.0m, and he says the back three has worked together since the play-offs. Two of the five own him.
verdicts.trigger: Being dropped for one of the six new arrivals. Jakirovic says loyalty counts, so it needs a bad result first.

verdicts.name: Mendy
verdicts.why: The third man in the back three with 24 points at £4.0m and 5.7% ownership. Nobody in the room owns him.
verdicts.trigger: Same as the other two. A goal conceded at Stamford Bridge tells you nothing. Two conceded at home to Everton does.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Took and scored the penalty at Brentford, after missing a Panenka there in January. 8 points on Mr CR7's bench.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks with Sunderland scoring. If the goals come from elsewhere, £5.9m buys a passer who does not shoot.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Danso made his debut in Sunderland's defence at Brentford, which was the trigger written on Thursday. Hume scored 1 and Mr CR7 started him.
verdicts.trigger: A start and a clean sheet with Danso and Fofana both fit. Arsenal at home next is not the week.

verdicts.name: Ballard
verdicts.why: Kept his place beside the debutant Danso, had a volley ruled out for Danso's offside, and finished with 4 points. Sir Fergie starts him.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the shirt to Fofana. Danso came in on Saturday and Ballard kept his place.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: Conceded to Leeds' first chance and then watched Leeds hit the bar and have a goal ruled out for inches. Three of the five start him.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet at Coventry next week. Coventry have not scored a top-flight goal since 2001, so it is the fixture he is bought for.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: His corner made the Vuskovic equaliser. 4 points on The Special One's bench, still in the advanced role.
verdicts.trigger: A return to left-back and a clean sheet. £4.7m for a makeshift winger is the wrong position at the wrong price.

verdicts.name: Groß
verdicts.why: Put a six-yard chance over the bar against Leeds and finished with 1 point. Both of his owners in the room started him.
verdicts.trigger: Two weeks without a return. This is one. At 33 the minutes are the question.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Put through twice in the first half at Brighton, dragged one wide and had the other stopped on the line by Dunk. 1 point, on four elevens and Sir Fergie's bench.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or Leeds changing the shape around him. Newcastle at home next.

verdicts.name: Bogle
verdicts.why: A tap-in and 14 points at Brighton, 22 for the season at £4.5m. 0.7% of the game own him.
verdicts.trigger: A second return in the next two. One haul from a right-back is one match.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: 2 points at home to Sunderland after Andrews changed three at half-time. The Guardian says Sangaré found it harder against Xhaka and Sadiki.
verdicts.trigger: Thiago rediscovering the shirt, or two blanks in a side that has drawn twice.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Kept his place while Collins went off with a calf strain and Kayode was hooked at half-time. 2 points.
verdicts.trigger: Two games conceding twice. Collins is flagged at 75% and Schuster impressed in his place.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: 18 points at £5.7m, and the Guardian says he found life harder against Xhaka than against Spurs. Nobody in the room owns him.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks. A midfielder scoring at this price is the cheapest way to fill an eleven.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Spurs' first clean sheet of the season at Forest, without a shot on target against. Everton at home next, and Mr CR7 starts him.
verdicts.trigger: Two goals conceded in a week. De Zerbi's plan is 60 minutes for Savio and Udogie, so the shape will change late in games.

verdicts.name: Van de Ven
verdicts.why: 9 points at Forest with the clean sheet and the bonus, at £5.0m. 3.7% of the game own him.
verdicts.trigger: Two games conceding twice. Spurs' defence looked settled on Saturday and their attack did not.

verdicts.name: Richarlison
verdicts.why: Left out of Spurs' 25-man squad. De Zerbi says he decided everything alone and cannot be registered again until January.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. A player outside the registered squad is an empty slot.

verdicts.name: N.Williams
verdicts.why: A clean sheet, bonus, and the goal VAR took off him for handball. 15 points at £5.0m.
verdicts.trigger: Two games conceding twice. Villa away next, and Villa have one shot on target this season.

verdicts.name: Delap
verdicts.why: Forest had two shots on target against Spurs and neither was his. 2 points at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: A start and a goal in the next two. Two starts and he replaces Igor Jesus as the Forest forward to own.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Villa kept their first clean sheet at Hull and Cash got 6 points on Le Professeur's bench. Villa have one shot on target in three games.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three with him playing all of them. This is one of the two.

verdicts.name: Suzuki
verdicts.why: Saved from Cho late on for a clean sheet and 10 points at Hull. £5.0m and 1.2% own him.
verdicts.trigger: A second clean sheet at home to Forest. Villa's defence has 10 new faces around it and one result.

verdicts.name: Mitchell
verdicts.why: Two goals at Fulham, the second in a fall while García missed the ball. 15 points at £4.5m and 4.9% own him.
verdicts.trigger: Any return in the next two. Two goals from a left-back is one afternoon and Palace conceded twice.

verdicts.name: Scott
verdicts.why: 24 points in three games at £6.0m, and Rose says he is proud he is a Bournemouth player. Nobody in the room owns him.
verdicts.trigger: A blank at home to Brentford. 24 points at 2.6% ownership is the room's blind spot.

verdicts.name: Tavernier
verdicts.why: Scored the opener at Newcastle, 21 points at £6.0m. 2.6% own him.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks. Scott is the one who makes the chances and Tavernier is the one who finishes them.

verdicts.name: King
verdicts.why: A deflected goal and the dummy that made Fulham's second, in front of Tuchel. 19 points at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: A return at Anfield next week. Fulham have conceded seven in three, so his side will chase games.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: Moyes says the squad is short and Everton have one senior striker. United at home today at £5.6m.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks against United and Spurs.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: 13 points at £6.5m, and Everton sold Ndiaye, Beto, Iroegbunam and Patterson in a week. The creation runs through him.
verdicts.trigger: Grealish taking the creative burden instead. One team sheet away and worth watching before it costs anything.

verdicts.name: Tarkowski

signals.action: 4.9% own him. Palace conceded twice, so this is two goals and no clean sheet. Ipswich at home next

signals.action: nobody in the room owns him. Brentford at home next, and he is the £6.0m midfielder the room has missed

signals.text: Villa's first clean sheet, at Hull, and 6 points on Le Professeur's bench.
signals.action: one clean sheet of the two his trigger asks for. Forest at home next

signals.action: more attacking involvement for a £5.7m defender with 20 points. Four of the five own him and Mr CR7 benches him today

signals.action: Le Professeur starts him ahead of Rogers. The 4.30 team sheet says whether that was right

signals.text: "There is the belief at Arsenal that Eze can in essence replace Martinelli on the left, albeit he is a different kind of player."
signals.action: £6.4m at 1.4%. A start against Chelsea and the price is wrong by a long way

signals.text: Arsenal have won three from three this season, Community Shield included, without conceding a goal.
signals.action: The Special One benched him on the wildcard behind a Hull goalkeeper who has also kept three. Arsenal go to Sunderland next while Hull go to Chelsea

signals.action: nobody in the room owns him and nobody should buy him this week

signals.text: Carrick called his performance against Ipswich immense. Baleba is flagged until 19 September.

signals.action: the place is safe and the minutes are not guaranteed. A cheap defender who might get rotated in the cup weeks

signals.action: sell or ignore. A player outside the squad list is an empty shirt at £5.9m

signals.text: Moyes: "We're going to need extra from them because we're short." Beto is sold and the Balogun deal collapsed, so he is the one senior striker. United at home at 2pm.
signals.action: the trigger was a striker arriving to take his shirt and nobody did. £5.6m

signals.action: United at home today, then Spurs away. Mr CR7 has him on his list and should keep him there

signals.text: Forest had two shots on target against Spurs, Gibbs-White's and McAtee's. 2 points.
signals.action: £5.5m at 0.8%. Villa away next. Two starts and a goal before he replaces Igor Jesus as the Forest forward to own

doctrine.text: Protecting your rank has a real cost. Price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template players are the default owns. Passing on them needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice. Sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul only tells you about one match. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week. Then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used. It is also the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up. Ignore the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position. Two of the room's bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro. None owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

An open window changes who plays before it changes who you should buy. Buy after the window shuts. It paid on 1 September. Two of the five went to bed owning an Everton midfielder and woke up owning a Manchester City substitute, and nobody who waited lost anything by waiting.

A cup tie tells you about the team sheet more than the result. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything. That is why a 35-year-old's header, a flagged striker's replacement and a vice-captain's absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need 90 minutes. Deadline day settled six calls here without a ball being kicked. They were the Liverpool winger, the Arsenal forward, the United left-back, the Everton striker, the Everton midfielder and the City left-back. A trigger only a scoreline can fire sits open through the weeks that decide the player.

A room that agrees has no protection against being wrong together. Not one of the five captained Haaland this week. The three who did in GW1 all moved off him. He scored twice at Palace before any of their captains had kicked a ball. Check what the room has agreed on, not only what it argues about. A week later all five captained him against Coventry. The room moves together in both directions. He scored against Coventry and all five got 18. Agreement was right this time and it gave nobody an edge.

Grade a rule by what it cost. Do not grade it by how sensible it sounded. D5 declined the £4.0m Hull defenders after one haul because they were flagged and it was one match. Two weeks on Hull have six points, two clean sheets, and the two best-scoring £4.0m defenders in the game. A rule that only ever says no stops being useful. Three weeks on it is three clean sheets, and D5 is retired.

A Bench Boost wants 15 players who start. It does not need a double gameweek. The page called Sir Fergie's chip premature on Saturday. By Sunday night every one of his 15 had played, and it had won him the week and the lead. Grade a chip by the team sheet it lands on. The calendar does not matter.

A player sold inside the league has not gone, he has just moved clubs. The price on his card does not move for a week either. Ndiaye is worth £6.0m in two of these squads this morning and is fourth in the queue at his new club. Read the new shirt, forget the old fee.

Do not grade a player on 45 minutes. Three sacks were reversed on Wednesday. They were a winger hooked at half-time, a defender who came on as a substitute, and a left-back who was never actually dropped. It happened again on Thursday. The Hull back four sacked on Monday for six deadline-day arrivals turns out to be the back four the head coach intends to keep. Wait for the second data point when the first one is a substitution.

The injury flag moves last, after the news is already out. Arsenal's centre-back missed Thursday's open training with Chelsea to come and carries no flag in the player file. The £75m midfielder beside him missed it too. A squad that is picked on Friday afternoon is reported on Thursday night and flagged on Saturday morning. Read the training ground first, then the file. It held on Saturday morning: the flag arrived two days after the training report, at 75%.

A verdict of squad depth needs a team sheet. Ndiaye was sacked on Monday as fourth in the queue at City and started his first game there on Saturday. D15 said read the new shirt. The page wrote the verdict before the shirt existed.

plan.outlook: Sunday of GW3, with Arsenal v Chelsea and Everton v United to come. Saturday belonged to The Special One's Wildcard, which leads the room's week by some distance with three players left to play. All five captained Haaland and he scored, so the armband separated nobody. Hull kept a third clean sheet and four Hull picks across three squads paid. Today, four of the five own Calafiori, all five own João Pedro and B.Fernandes, Mr CR7 benches the Arsenal defender and Le Professeur benches Rogers. The GW4 deadline is Saturday 12 September and the fixture is the Manchester derby, so the captaincy question for the room is Haaland away or B.Fernandes at home.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline on 2 January. Three have been played in three weeks. Le Professeur's Bench Boost returned six points in GW1. Sir Fergie's returned the best week anyone has had, and the lead, in GW2. The Special One's Wildcard came in GW3 and is winning the week with three players to come. Xabi and Mr CR7 hold all four of theirs.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.

Saturday of a gameweek one fixture old. Upgraded Cherki to nailed on the start his trigger asked for, plus two goals at Selhurst Park, and recorded that not one of the five captained Haaland before he scored twice. Moved Guéhi back towards a buy once Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back. Settled Watkins on the £50m Al-Hilal sale and Martinez on Villa confirming the Chelsea deal. Opened Foden, O'Reilly, Diouf, Delap and Muñoz. Recommended no transfer again, on the grounds that the window shuts on Tuesday and the GW3 deadline is the Friday after it — the first week of the season in which waiting costs nothing. Minted D12 on the armband.

Saturday's five fixtures settled four open triggers and opened a hole. Upgraded Tarkowski to solid on the late goal at Bournemouth, exactly the trigger written on Thursday. Sacked Tonali, whose trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle and who was substituted in a 2-0 defeat, and sacked Gravenberch, who was left out of the pivot rather than keeping a clean sheet in it. Moved Igor Jesus back to watch after he started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, and cooled Delap for the same reason. Cooled Kerkez after he was taken off on 71 minutes, and cooled Woltemade after Wissa scored at Spurs and Napoli were reported to want him on loan. Settled Sánchez and Muñoz by transfer. Opened Isak, Gibbs-White, Elanga, Wissa, Scott and the three Hull picks. Minted D13 against the brain's own D5: the £4.0m Hull defenders it declined after one haul now have two clean sheets behind them and thirty-six points between them. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday.

Gameweek 2 settled everything except Villa v Arsenal. Marked the brain's own Bench Boost rule under review after Sir Fergie played one in a single gameweek and won the week and the lead with it — D14. Upgraded B.Fernandes on a hat-trick that fired his blank trigger the other way, and upgraded Maguire, Lammens, Schade, Calvert-Lewin, Wissa, Ajayi and Tzolakis. Sacked Lacroix on the exact trigger written on Thursday — a clean sheet against a depleted Brighton — after Chelsea conceded three and reached eighteen games without one. Sacked Caicedo, who came off in tears after eleven minutes, Kerkez a week early on the substitution rather than the missed start, Welbeck on an unused bench at 4-3, and Woltemade once Wissa started and scored. Cooled Ndiaye with Spurs in advanced talks, Semenyo on one assist at £8.5m, De Cuyper on an advanced role that is not the position he was bought for, and Havertz on Arsenal chasing Álvarez. Opened Rashford, Neto and Groß. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday, with the deadline three days behind it.

First run with the window shut. Recommended the room's first transfers of the season. Ndiaye out for Mr CR7 and Le Professeur after his £65m move to Manchester City, and Aït-Nouri out for The Special One on City calling him third-choice left-back. Reversed three sacks that deadline day settled the other way. Gakpo stays after Liverpool rejected £80m. Shaw keeps his place after United failed to sign a left-back. Barry becomes Everton's only striker after the Balogun deal collapsed. Sacked Tzolis on a 4/10 and a half-time substitution, and Konsa on coming off the bench rather than starting. Cooled Cherki, Foden and Semenyo on City signing two more attackers, and cooled the whole Hull back four on six deadline-day arrivals and the sale of a defender who had played all three games. Promoted D9 to doctrine on the evidence it just produced, retired D6 into D14, and minted D15 on players sold inside the league.

Deadline eve. Reversed three of Monday's own sacks after reading the window post-mortems. Tzolis was graded on 45 minutes, but impressed in the Community Shield and on the opening day. Konsa was signed because Saliba and Timber are injured, and the man ahead of him limped off. Kerkez stays because Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola knows him from Bournemouth. Upgraded Gvardiol to nailed on City saying O'Reilly moves into midfield, which reverses last week's trigger. Downgraded Szoboszlai on Liverpool naming him as right-back cover, and Gakpo on Barcola's likely debut at Ipswich. Upgraded Ajayi on the flag coming off. Recommended captaincy calls rather than transfers for three of the five, and minted D16. A verdict written on 45 minutes proves nothing.

Deadline day, window shut. Read the training ground rather than the player file. Mosquera and Bruno Guimarães both missed Arsenal's open session on Thursday. Downgraded Mosquera without a flag, moved Konsa and White up, and told Le Professeur to promote Konsa off his bench rather than spend a transfer. Reversed Monday's cooling of the Hull back four after Jakirovic said the six deadline-day arrivals must earn shirts, and put Ajayi back on the house list. Opened Barcola, Guéhi and Bruno G., and sacked Richarlison outright. He was left out of Spurs' registered Premier League squad. Upgraded Verbruggen on Rodon's eight-to-ten-week hamstring and Leeds improvising at centre-back. Repeated the Ndiaye transfer for the two owners and the Aït-Nouri sale for The Special One. Minted D17. The flag moves last.

Saturday, one fixture into GW3. Friday night at Ipswich settled three of Thursday's triggers the right way. Kerkez kept the clean sheet his trigger asked for, Gakpo made both goals with Barcola on the bench, and Szoboszlai played in midfield while Araujo debuted at right-back. Upgraded all three to solid and opened Isak, Jacquet and Araujo. Read the deadline. All five captained Haaland and The Special One played his Wildcard from last place with 12 changes. Mr CR7 sold Ndiaye and started Calvert-Lewin as recommended. Le Professeur sold Konsa the day before every predicted Arsenal XI named him. Downgraded Shaw on a hamstring fitness test, Hume on a predicted Sunderland XI without him, and Dewsbury-Hall on Grealish's return. Downgraded Mosquera again as the flag arrived on Saturday morning, two days after the training report, which is D17 holding once. Rewrote the Team radar for the Saturday and Sunday team sheets. No transfer recommended. The GW4 deadline is a week away and Sunday's derby decides four Arsenal and Chelsea calls.

Saturday of GW3, one match in. Friday night settled three Liverpool triggers the right way. Gakpo started and made both goals while Barcola came off the bench, so Gakpo goes up to solid. Kerkez kept the clean sheet his trigger asked for and goes up. Szoboszlai played in midfield with Araujo on debut at right-back and goes up. Opened Isak, Jacquet, Araujo, Wirtz, Frimpong, Diop, Dedić, Egan, Raya, Mainoo and Delap. Downgraded Mosquera again once the 75% flag arrived, two days after the training report, which is D17 holding. Noted that all five captained Haaland a week after none did, and added it to D12. Read the Newcastle team sheet: Hornicek in goal, Hall and Elanga starting, Fernandez-Pardo on the bench. Recorded The Special One's Wildcard at 16 points after one match, with Raya on the bench behind Tzolakis, and Le Professeur selling Konsa the day before Mosquera was flagged. Set the GW4 question for the whole room as the derby captaincy. No roast: the gameweek is live.

Sunday of GW3, seven fixtures played. Saturday settled a dozen triggers. Cherki went up to solid on a second start, Guéhi on a return to centre-back, Kinsky on Spurs' first clean sheet, and E.Le Fée on the penalty at Brentford. Hume went to sack once Danso made his debut. Ndiaye came back from sack to watch after starting at the Etihad five days after both owners sold him, and D18 records the miss. Semenyo's trigger asked for a goal and he produced the assist, so he holds at watch. Verbruggen's clean-sheet trigger did not fire. Opened O'Reilly on the warm-up injury, Enzo Fernández and Foden on the City team sheet, Mendy, Ballard, Van de Ven, N.Williams, Suzuki, Mitchell, Scott, Tavernier, King, Bogle and Barnes. Retired D5 on Hull's third clean sheet. Rewrote the Team radar for Porto, the cup ties and the derby week. No transfer recommended before Sunday's two games.

why.name: Tzolakis
why.text: Only The Special One has him. Hull have kept two clean sheets from two, and Villa arrive on Saturday having scored no goals in two games. A £4.6m keeper at home to a side that has not scored is the start of this team.

why.name: Ajayi
why.text: Mr CR7 owns him and the other four don't. Two clean sheets and 20 points at £4.1m. Villa at home is the fixture that keeps him in, and the price is what lets Isak and Fernandes fit in the same side.

why.name: Mendy
why.text: None of you own him. Two clean sheets and 16 points at £4.0m beside Ajayi. Two Hull defenders and the keeper is three from one club against a Villa attack with no goals this season. That bet is taken on purpose.

why.name: Gvardiol
why.text: Mr CR7 and The Special One hold him. City host Coventry, who have lost both games without scoring, and Gvardiol has 14 points from two. The clean sheet is the likeliest in the round and he is the City defender who pushes forward.

why.name: Hall
why.text: None of you own him. Newcastle beat Spurs 2-0 last week with a clean sheet and Hall has 14 points from two games. Bournemouth come to St James' Park having scored once in each of their two games.

why.name: Gakpo
why.text: Only The Special One has him. 17 points from two games at £7.1m, and Liverpool go to Ipswich, who let in five at Old Trafford last Saturday. He is cheaper than Szoboszlai's owners would expect and has outscored him.

why.name: M.Sangaré
why.text: None of you own him. 18 points from two at £5.7m, with Brentford beating Spurs 3-0 and drawing at Leeds. Sunderland at home is the third fixture in a row where Brentford should have the ball.

why.name: Isak
why.text: None of you own him. £9.0m and 10 points from two draws, both with Liverpool scoring twice. Ipswich conceded five to United a week ago. He takes the third forward slot over João Pedro because of who each of them plays.

why.name: Barry
why.text: None of you own him. First off the bench, £5.6m, on Everton's penalties, and at home to a United defence that shipped two at Hull. He plays if one of the front two drops out.

why.name: Kayode
why.text: None of you own him. 15 points from two at £4.6m and the first defender off the bench. He covers Hall if Newcastle rest anyone before Bournemouth.

why.name: Gomez
why.text: None of you own him. A £5.0m Brighton midfielder with 11 points who plays. He is the fifth midfielder and the cover, nothing more.

why.name: Steele
why.text: None of you own him and he does not play. He is the £4.0m that lets Tzolakis start, and a ghost manager with no transfers does not need a second keeper who plays.

left_out.name: João Pedro
left_out.text: All five of you own him and he is the most captained man in the game. This week Chelsea go to Arsenal, who have not conceded in two games. Isak costs £1.3m more and plays Ipswich. Ted leaves him out for one week and for that reason only.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: None of you own him. 20 points from two and on Chelsea's penalties. Arsenal away kept him out of this squad. Hull at home next week gets him in.

watchlist.name: Saka
watchlist.note: None of you own him. Chelsea have conceded five goals in two games, and Saka has 20 points and the penalties. He lost the slot to Gakpo on price. A Chelsea defence that leaks again on Saturday puts him in.

watchlist.name: Guéhi
watchlist.note: None of you own him. He would be in the side this week but for the three-per-club rule at City. Gvardiol got the slot because he goes forward more.
